text:
Taylor S.: I was on unpaid parental leave during open enrollment and missed the window. I need to switch to the HDHP + HSA and increase my dependent care FSA for next year. Is there any way to make changes now?

Asha (People Ops): Hi Taylor  sorry about the timing. Short answer: open enrollment changes are generally final unless you have a qualifying life event (QLE) or the carrier grants an exception. Being on leave alone is usually not a QLE. Why did you miss it? was there a system error or a documented leave that prevented access?

Taylor S.: HR portal showed me as "on leave" and I couldn't access benefit election pages. I have the approved leave paperwork from People Ops and the manager signed return-to-work note.

Asha (People Ops): OK that helps. If you couldn't access the enrollment system due to a Redwood administrative status error, we can request an exception. Please upload the leave approval and any screenshots showing blocked access. If it's a carrier-level decision they sometimes approve exceptions for administrative errors.

Taylor S.: Uploaded leave_approval_1932109999.pdf and blocked_access_screenshot.png

Benefits Bot: Upload received from Taylor S. File IDs: up_1932101001, up_1932101002. Status: awaiting manual review.

Max (Benefits Ops): I'll review docs and submit an exception request to carriers. Quick heads up: even if carrier approves a mid-cycle plan change, FSAs follow IRS rules. Dependent care FSA midyear increases are typically allowed only with a QLE; carriers might allow a plan election change but payroll/IRS rules for FSA are stricter. We can request an HSA/HDHP switch and see if FSA increase is permitted, but plan may deny the FSA change.

Lina (Payroll): Payroll impact: if we change elections mid-plan year, deductions will be recalculated pro-rata. For DC FSA, if increase is allowed, it'll be spread over remaining paychecks. If denied, you could consider a Section 125 plan amendment only if IRS rules permit. We'll need Benefits' approval and the effective date to update payroll.

Taylor S.: If carrier denies FSA increase, is there any retro remedy like a reimbursement for dependent care paid out-of-pocket?

Max (Benefits Ops): If FSA change is denied, no retro increases are permitted under typical IRC Section 125 rules. Reimbursements are only from the contributed balance. You might be able to claim the dependent care tax credit on your tax return for eligible expenses, but that's separate from FSA. We can put you in touch with payroll/tax guidance if needed.

Asha (People Ops): I'll attach a short cover letter when I file the carrier exception: mention system access issue, include leave approval, screenshot, manager note. Carriers usually respond in 5-10 business days. If they approve the HDHP switch, effective date is usually the first of next month; sometimes carriers permit retro to Jan 1 for open enrollment mistakes but that's rare.

Taylor S.: Thanks  uploaded manager_note_1932101003.pdf. Anything else you need?

Benefits Bot: Upload received File ID: up_1932101004 Status: queued for review.

Max (Benefits Ops): Good. I'll submit the exception request now and post the carrier case# when available. Lina, if approved please prepare payroll proration for Taylor.

Lina (Payroll): Will do. Taylor, once Benefits confirms effective date I'll calculate the per-paycheck deduction change and DM you an estimate.

Asha (People Ops): Filing exception now. If carrier denies, we'll explore alternate options (open enrollment through special company policy in exceptional cases is rare but possible for next plan year). I'll update thread when carrier responds.

Taylor S.: Appreciate the help. Fingers crossed.

Max (Benefits Ops): Case submitted to carrier at 1932101007. Expect response in ~7 business days.

Asha (People Ops): Thanks everyone. Taylor, I'll keep you posted here and DM any sensitive details.
